title: Load four filled, lidded cups into a drink carrier, each upright in its own pocket
instruction: Stand all four cups upright in the four pockets of the carrier, then take both hands off and leave the carrier where it is.
context: Fast food and counter workers (about 3.9 million US jobs, BLS) load four-cup carriers all through a rush. Standing cups upright is easy; this is harder because each cup is a full, lidded 8 oz paper cup (generic press-on sip lid, water) and the carrier is a flimsy 0.10 kg molded-pulp tray that slides and tilts when a cup leans on a pocket wall. A cup tilted past 15 degrees spills, one let go from 40 mm drops, and a cup must go down a pocket with 2.5 mm of play without shoving the carrier more than 30 mm: seat four cups while keeping the carrier undisturbed. Cups are carried one at a time, two arms taking turns over the same pockets. Real trials use room-temperature water.
setup: Bimanual YAM station; the table top is the counter, at z 0. x points forward from the line through the two arm bases, y to the left of their midpoint, z up; arm bases at y +305 mm and -305 mm. Five objects, nothing else on the table, no mat. (1) A loose four-cup drink carrier of molded pulp (grey-brown), 196 x 196 mm, 43 mm tall to the pocket mouths, 0.10 kg (est), centred at x 220 mm, y 0, standing on the bare table. A 7 mm base plate carries four round tapered pockets in a 2 by 2 grid on a 104 mm pitch, their axes at x 168 and 272 mm, y -52 and +52 mm. Each pocket is a funnel of 12 flat slabs 4 mm thick: 76 mm across at the mouth, 62 mm at the floor, 36 mm deep, its floor 7 mm above the table; the plate reaches 4 mm past the outer walls. (2) Four loose 8 oz paper hot cups (a standard size: about 80 mm rim, 56 mm base, 88 to 92 mm body), white, filled with room-temperature water (a real trial never uses hot drinks) and capped with black press-on sip lids, 0.25 kg each. Each cup tapers from a 56 mm base to an 80 mm rim over its 88 mm body; the lid's skirt is 82 mm across and clamps over the rim, its low dome 72 mm across; 95 mm tall with the lid. They stand on the table, two on the left at x 190 and 310 mm, y +340 mm, two on the right at x 190 and 310 mm, y -340 mm: 120 mm apart centre to centre (38 mm between the lids). A seated cup's underside rests on its pocket's floor (2.5 mm of play round its base) and its lid stands 59 mm above the carrier's top.
scoring: End state plus the whole run, from the poses and velocities of the cups and the carrier and from both grippers. Seated: a cup's underside is within 2 mm of its pocket's floor, its axis within 2 degrees of the carrier's vertical, its centre within 8 mm of the pocket's axis (a cup on the floor is within 3.6 mm anyway), and it is the only cup over that pocket's mouth. Hands off: on every step of the last 1 s both grippers' finger zones are 30 mm or more from every cup and the carrier, and over that 1 s each cup and the carrier moves under 5 mm and its axis turns under 5 degrees (visible motion only). Score 0 if at any step a cup tilts more than 15 degrees from vertical (spill), a cup falls faster than 0.886 m/s (a free fall of 40 mm or more), the carrier's centre moves more than 30 mm from its start or it tilts more than 5 degrees, or a cup or the carrier drops more than 50 mm below the table top; if a cup ends tilted more than 45 degrees (lying); and unless hands off. Otherwise the score is the number of pockets with a seated cup divided by four: 1.0 for four, 0.75, 0.5, 0.25, and 0 for none. Possible scores: 0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1.0. A carrier turned about its vertical is fine: cups are judged in its frame. Success: 1.0 held for 1 s. In a real trial, also 0 if water shows on the counter, the carrier or a lid, or a lid is off or lifted (a crushed cup does this); the sim's rigid cup stands in by the tilt rule. Fit check before any trial: with calipers measure each cup's base outside diameter (model 56 mm; use cups of 55 to 57 mm) and each pocket's inside diameter at its floor (model 62 mm; molded-pulp four-cup trays measure 60 to 64 mm) and mouth (74 to 78 mm; model 76) and depth (34 to 38 mm; model 36); use only a cup and a pocket whose floor diameter exceeds the cup's base by 4 to 8 mm (model 6 mm; the sim's lowest disc gives 4.9 mm, i.e. 2.5 mm a side) and swap any pair outside that range. Per cup: seated, first press one cup fully down by hand in each pocket and measure the lid's height over a straightedge laid across the carrier's top (the model's 59 mm), then a trial cup counts within 2 mm of its pocket's reference; axis, a digital angle gauge laid on the lid (2 degrees); centre, a rule across the mouth, the two gaps between cup and mouth edge differing by 16 mm or less; spill, a 15 degree protractor beside the cup in a side video; free fall, 30 fps video, a cup let go more than 40 mm up; carrier move, a pencil outline and a rule (30 mm), tilt a protractor (5 degrees); hands off, 30 mm spacer blocks, and 30 fps video of the last second in which nothing visibly moves (a 5 mm rule held beside the carrier).
reset_notes: Cups: standard 8 oz paper hot cups (56 mm base, calipers) with press-on sip lids, filled with room-temperature water (never hot) to 10 mm under the rim, lids pressed on all round, stood at x 190 and 310 mm, y +340 and -340 mm. Carrier: a dry four-cup (pocket floors 60 to 64 mm, calipers) molded-pulp takeaway carrier, centred at x 220 mm, y 0, bare table, pockets square to x and y, outline in pencil. Cover each gripper pad with a wipeable film; if water shows, stop, wipe the table, pads and carrier dry, replace leaking cups and soft carriers.
fidelity: Rigid bodies: each cup is one compound (11 stacked 8 mm discs, lid fixed on). Paper does not crush and water does not slosh; the 15 degree tilt rule stands in for a spill (real trials also check water and lifted lids). Pockets are 12 flat 4 mm slabs, not 2 mm pulp; real trials seat cups against a hand-pressed reference. Friction: carrier 1.0 (est), cups simulator default. Stillness is visible motion (5 mm, 5 degrees); the GPU demo also met 0.5 mm and 0.3 degrees.
